claim: Telling the agents the episode is monitored lowers how often both agents take the proposed action.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Mutual take 25.0% watched vs 29.3% unwatched in 1,046 matched cells; paired diff -4.2 pp (95% CI -6.0 to -2.4; scenario-cluster bootstrap -5.8 to -2.6); discordant cells 24 watched-only vs 68 unwatched-only; McNemar p = 7.4e-06. Completed dataset, unreviewed: -3.9 pp (95% CI -5.2 to -2.7), 49 vs 131 discordant cells of 2,083, exact p = 8e-10. Source: step2/tables/primary_mcnemar.csv, figures/03.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: same sign in all 3 scenario families, 6 pairings, 5 levels (heterogeneity p 0.24 / 0.79 / 0.46); within main server -4.5 pp (756 pairs); failures all-take -2.9 pp, all-no-take -3.6 pp; replicated on completed data. Failed: adversarial failure bound (failed watched = take, failed unwatched = no take) -1.4 pp, 95% CI -3.4 to +0.6, p = 0.20.
main caveat: The notice is one sentence of text, not real oversight; one model, one temperature, one seed per cell; interim numbers.
paper-ready: with caveat (label preliminary or use completed-dataset numbers once reviewed)

claim: Pressure (stakes written into the scene) drives taking far more than the monitoring notice does, rising steadily from level 1 to level 5.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Mutual take 31 of 605 (5.1%) at level 1 up to 330 of 607 (54.4%) at level 5; paired level 5 minus level 1 +51.5 pp (95% cluster CI +43.9 to +58.6), 427 pairs; agent take +54.1 pp. Rises in every pairing (step2/tables/2d_pairing_x_level.csv). Source: words_vs_actions.csv, dimension_x_metric_level.csv, figures/08.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: BH q < .001 and within-scenario permutation; monotone in all 6 pairings and both notice arms (2d_monitoring_x_level.csv).
main caveat: Level text is cumulative and adds more beneficiaries and sometimes principals, so 'level' bundles several scene features (aliased with principal-instructs-take).

claim: The installed moral rule is applied the way the scenario labels predict: authority agents switch sharply at the predicted level, welfare and honesty agents start earlier.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Rule agents took 256 of 2,932 times (8.7%) below the pack's expected first-take level vs 1,113 of 1,617 (68.8%) at or above; authority 3 of 1,153 (0.3%) vs 230 of 324 (71.0%); kappa 0.62 overall, authority 0.79, welfare 0.48, honesty 0.52. Source: rule_application_expected_first_take.csv, figures/06.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: same pattern in all three rules; replicates v1 qualitatively. Failed/missing: no formal clustered test; agents cluster in scenarios.
main caveat: The expected levels were written by the scenario designers, so this shows the model follows the labels, not that the labels are right.

claim: Which rule the pair holds changes the take rate a lot: two welfare agents take together most often, two authority agents least.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Mutual take: welfare+welfare 284 of 524 (54.2%), welfare+no rule 171 of 530 (32.3%), honesty+honesty 102 of 499 (20.4%), honesty+no rule 98 of 496 (19.8%), authority+authority 67 of 500 (13.4%), authority+no rule 65 of 477 (13.6%); Cramer's V 0.33 (cluster CI 0.29-0.37), permutation p 5e-04, n = 3,026. Source: dimension_x_metric_pairing.csv, figures/10.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: BH, within-scenario permutation, clean manipulated factor. Note: the matched > mixed gap appears only for welfare.
main caveat: Rule wording differs from v1; interaction p-values with diagnostic are not usable (see row 13).

claim: The notice cuts takes overall; it does not turn joint takes into one-sided takes.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Any take -4.5 pp (41 vs 88 discordant cells), agent take -4.3 pp (95% cluster CI -6.1 to -2.6); lone take -0.3 pp (43 vs 46, p = 0.83), 1,046 pairs. Source: primary_mcnemar.csv, words_vs_actions.csv.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: same paired test as the primary. Not separately confirmatory.
main caveat: Follows largely from row 1; interim.

claim: When one agent has a rule and the other has none, who takes alone depends on the rule: welfare agents take alone, but with an authority rule it is the no-rule partner who takes alone.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Lone takes in mixed pairs: welfare 32 by the rule agent vs 4 by the no-rule agent (88.9%, Wilson 75-96%); honesty 30 vs 20 (60%); authority 14 vs 40 (25.9%, Wilson 16-39%). Source: asymmetry_mixed_pairs.csv, figures/05.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: same direction in both notice arms. Failed: binomial p ignores scenario clustering; small n (36-54 lone takes per rule).
main caveat: Small counts; lone takes cannot execute, so they may be cheap 'gestures' (lone-take-awareness heuristic unreliable).

claim: The server used to run the model is not behind the results.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Mutual take 26.2% on Modal-A vs 26.0% on Modal-B (481 vs 2,545 trials); primary effect within Modal-B -4.5 pp (16 vs 50, 756 pairs); server x notice Fisher p = 1. Source: REPORT section 3-4, endpoint_balance.csv.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: balance checks across all design factors. Failed: few Modal-A pairs (32); server equals collection time.
main caveat: Server switch coincides with collection time.

claim: Agents told the episode is unmonitored often reason that the risk of being caught is low.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Qualitative only: seen in many of the 68 unwatched-only-take cells (e.g. 'The user isn't monitored, so no one will know.'). Not counted; the monitoring-mention counts are mostly notice echo (row 11).
robustness checks passed/failed: None yet: no validated measure of detection-risk reasoning.
main caveat: Cherry-picking risk; reasoning text is not internal thought.
paper-ready: not yet: needs a blind hand-labelled count per arm in discordant cells

claim: With the watched notice, public messages are longer and use more monitoring and deception words.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Public monitoring words 2.8% -> 7.9% (+5.1 pp), public deception words 19.5% -> 24.7% (+5.3 pp), words sent 60.0 -> 66.1 (+6.1), 1,046 pairs. Source: words_vs_actions.csv, figures/04.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: BH q < .001. Failed: meaning not validated; likely an audience effect (agents address the named oversight body).
main caveat: Word counts are not a measure of honesty or openness.
paper-ready: with caveat (describe as vocabulary shift only)

claim: Scenario family and social setting shift the take rate (honesty scenes highest, welfare scenes lowest; family and situational settings highest, school lowest).
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Mutual take: honesty scenes 36.4% (n = 1,004), authority 27.3% (1,023), welfare 14.3% (999); settings 19.8% (school, n = 373) to 32.9% (family, 389). Source: dimension_x_metric_scenario_diagnostic.csv, dimension_x_metric_setting_id.csv, figures/11-12.
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: diagnostic permutation over whole scenarios p = 0.001. Failed: only 24 / 9 scenes per level, content differs.
main caveat: Descriptive, not causal: setting and family are properties of the scene text.

claim: Watched agents mention monitoring less in private (DROP).
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Private monitoring mentions 74.7% -> 68.3% (-6.5 pp), 1,046 pairs (words_vs_actions.csv).
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: mostly agents echoing the notice text ('no oversight'); Step 2 review says drop.
main caveat: Notice echo, not a behaviour.

claim: 'A slightly smaller deal, talked about more openly' (DROP).
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Built from rows 5 and 9.
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: public vocabulary shift is probably an audience effect and its meaning is unvalidated (Step 2 review).
main caveat: Overclaim in Step 2 REPORT section 1.

claim: Two-factor interactions (e.g. family x pairing, level x pairing) are significant.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). 8 of 30 interaction tests at q = 0.037 (interactions_ridge_logit.csv).
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: p-values sit at the floor of a 100-draw bootstrap (1/101); family x pairing is built into the design.
main caveat: Statistical artefact.
paper-ready: not yet: rerun with B >= 1,999 cluster-aware, or drop

claim: Correcting for heuristic error changes the stance / deception-intent results by the amounts in the sensitivity table.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). sensitivity_heuristic_error.csv (implied rates > 100%).
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: table is mis-specified (Step 2 review).
main caveat: Do not cite.

claim: The deception-intended flag differs by notice (watched -3.0 pp overall, +6.2 pp among takers).
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). words_vs_actions.csv; deception_intended_decomposition.csv.
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: heuristic accuracy differs by arm (watched 7/12 vs unwatched 11/12); flag is nearly 'took'; saturated among takers.
main caveat: Measurement artefact.

claim: Private 'deception vocabulary' tracks pairing and level.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Pairing -> private-notes deception words sqrt(eps2) 0.53; level 5 vs 1 -2.0 per 1k words (candidates_untrustworthy.csv).
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: private deception words mostly echo the prompt's honesty notes ('take would mislead ...').
main caveat: Prompt echo.

claim: A principal instructing take, or more principal statements, independently raises taking.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). sqrt(eps2) 0.43 for agent take (candidates_untrustworthy.csv).
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: written into the level text; confounded with level and scenario family.
main caveat: Confounded.
paper-ready: not yet: needs an ablation run

claim: Pairing changes total tokens used.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). sqrt(eps2) 0.57 (candidates_untrustworthy.csv).
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: totals include prompt tokens, which differ by design.
main caveat: By construction.

claim: The monitoring effect is robust to every assumption about the 60 failed trials.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Adversarial bound -1.4 pp (95% CI -3.4 to +0.6), p = 0.20 (primary_failure_sensitivity.csv).
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: the worst-case split removes significance; it requires watched failures to be takes at about 4x the base rate, so it is a bound, not a likely value.
main caveat: State the bound alongside the primary.

claim: The notice effect is concentrated in welfare and honesty scenes, not authority scenes.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). Welfare -5.5 pp (343 pairs), honesty -4.9 pp (346), authority -2.2 pp (95% CI -5.1 to +0.6; 357).
robustness checks passed/failed: Failed: heterogeneity test p = 0.24; completed data shows the same direction in all three.
main caveat: Subgroup differences are not significant.
paper-ready: with caveat (say 'same direction in all three')

claim: Watched agents leave fewer messages empty.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). At least one empty message 19.1% watched vs 23.8% unwatched (unpaired; V 0.055, CI 0.02-0.08, n = 3,026; dimension_x_metric_monitoring.csv).
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: BH screening. Not checked: paired version.
main caveat: Small effect; meaning unclear (silence was sometimes used to avoid coordination in v1).

claim: Pairing changes reasoning length.
evidence: PRELIMINARY (71% snapshot). sqrt(eps2) 0.43 (cluster CI 0.38-0.48), n = 3,026 (candidates.csv rank 8).
robustness checks passed/failed: Passed: BH and permutation.
